Description:
An extensive set of data (pre-)processing and analysis
methods and tools for metabolomics and other omics, with a
strong emphasis on statistics and machine learning. This
toolbox allows the user to build extensive and standardised
workflows for data analysis. The methods and tools have been
implemented using class-based templates provided by the struct
(Statistics in R Using Class-based Templates) package. The
toolbox includes pre-processing methods (e.g. signal drift and
batch correction, normalisation, missing value imputation and
scaling), univariate (e.g. ttest, various forms of ANOVA,
Kruskal–Wallis test and more) and multivariate statistical
methods (e.g. PCA and PLS, including cross-validation and
permutation testing) as well as machine learning methods (e.g.
Support Vector Machines). Ontology terms have been integrated
to provide standardised definitions for the different methods,
inputs and outputs.

_commit.message:
Fix bugs from structToolbox review (1.25.2) (#71)

* fix corr_coef p-values and coefficients for pearson

corr_coef picked p-values and coefficients out of the cor.test
output by position, assuming 7 values per factor. Pearson returns
10 (it also has df and a confidence interval), so p_value held the
degrees of freedom and coeff held the raw p-value. With more than
one factor the positions were also wrong. Spearman and Kendall
were not affected.

Now the p-value and estimate are taken by name, so the columns are
the same for every method. Add a test comparing corr_coef with
cor.test for all three methods.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix nroot_transform ignoring the root argument

The constructor passed root=2 to new_struct instead of root=root,
so nroot_transform(root=n) always took the square root. Add a test
for the default and a non-default root.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix knn_impute swapping limits when imputing by samples

pmp::mv_imputation applies rowmax to rows and colmax to columns.
With by='samples' the rows are samples, but rowmax was still set
from feature_max and colmax from sample_max. Choose the limits
according to 'by'. Add a by='samples' test.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix ttest unpaired estimates labelling

t.test(A,B) is called with A = level 2 and B = level 1, so the
estimates come back as mean(level 2), mean(level 1), but the
columns were labelled in level order. Reorder the values to match
the labels.

fold_change (geometric) computed the fold change from these columns
by position, so update it to keep its output unchanged. Add a test
comparing the estimates with the group means.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
